Thanks again for the time today — great to see the Cerebrum demo and the LLM use cases you outlined. Per our ask on the call, a short list of follow-ups that will help us produce a recommended Dedicated configuration (GPU flavor, pool size, and concurrency strategy):

1) Traffic profile
   - Steady-state TPS (requests/sec) you expect during normal day-to-day?
   - Peak TPS and typical burst duration (e.g., 3–10 minutes vs sustained hours)?
   - Typical concurrency (how many requests you expect to execute simultaneously under normal load)?

2) Token profile
   - Avg prompt tokens / avg completion tokens
   - Fraction of requests that are short chat (<= 128 tokens) vs long generation (> 512 tokens)

3) Latency & SLOs
   - p95 and p99 latency SLOs (server-side generation time) you need; any maximum tail limit?

4) State/cache
   - Do you require persistent KV cache across requests/sessions (yes/no)? How large is context (average conversation length in tokens)?

5) Security/deployment constraints
   - Any regulatory or networking requirements that push you to Private (VPC) vs Hosted vs Dedicated?

Attached: simple sizing template (capacity_sizing_template.xlsx) — if you can fill the TPS/token fields (or paste numbers inline) we’ll run a rapid model-by-model sizing and return two SKU options (cost-optimized and latency-optimized).

Suggested next step: technical deep-dive with our infra/ops (Laura + Logan) — 30 minutes to validate ingestion patterns and KV/cache needs. I can propose slots for Mon/Tue next week.

Thanks —

Karthik — thanks for the clear list. Answers below (quick paste from our internal ops measurement):

1) Traffic profile
   - Steady-state TPS: ~6 req/sec (even distribution across our EU/US user base)
   - Peak TPS: observed bursts up to ~70 req/sec during feature launches; typical bursts last 5–12 minutes
   - Typical concurrency: 18–25 concurrent inferences when steady; up to ~120 concurrent during peak bursts

2) Token profile
   - Avg prompt tokens: 85
   - Avg completion tokens: 160 (but ~15% of requests are long-form generation ~800–1,200 tokens)
   - Mix: ~75% short chat (<128 tokens), ~25% long generation

3) Latency & SLOs
   - Goal p95 server-side <= 150ms for short chat; for long generations we can tolerate higher (p95 <= 1.0s)

4) State/cache
   - We would like persistent KV cache per user session for chat history (median context ~1,200 tokens; some power users up to ~6,000 tokens)

5) Security/deployment constraints
   - Data residency: primary customer data must remain in US regions for now. We are evaluating VPC/private for sensitive accounts but would consider Dedicated in Redwood-hosted US regions first.

We can join a deep-dive Tuesday 2027-05-11 10:00–10:30 PT if that works for you + your ops team. Also looping in our procurement lead (Marty) to start contractual/PO conversation.

—Samira
Director of Product, Cerebrum Labs

Samira — perfect, thanks for the numbers; that’s very actionable. Quick read and initial recommendations before the Tuesday deep-dive:

- Traffic & concurrency
  Given steady 6 TPS and peak bursts ~70 TPS with up to ~120 concurrent inferences, we’ll likely recommend a Dedicated pool sized for peak-burst elasticity plus a small buffer. Two viable approaches:
  1) Capacity headroom (latency-optimized): Provision GPU capacity to sustain 70–80 TPS with p95 targets. This reduces cold-starts and keeps per-request latency low.
  2) Autoscaling + burst policy (cost-optimized): Smaller baseline pool (covers steady ~6 TPS) with aggressive burst capacity for short peaks. Works well if bursts remain <15 min.

- Token mix implications
  The mix (75% short chat, 25% long form) argues for hybrid batching: smaller batch windows for short chat (to meet 150ms p95) and larger, slightly higher-latency paths for long-form jobs. Our runtime supports routing by request class.

- GPU recommendation (initial)
  For your workload I’d propose two SKU options we’ll present formally:
  A) H100-heavy cluster (fewer nodes, highest throughput) — better for long generations and very high-concurrency bursts; higher unit cost but fewer machines to manage.
  B) A100-optimized cluster with more nodes (good latency characteristics with smaller batch windows; typically better cost for chat-heavy workloads).

Notes on KV/cache: with session contexts up to 6k tokens we recommend enabling per-session KV caching with a node-local cache tier; this reduces repeated token decoding costs and keeps latencies tight for chat. We’ll need to validate memory footprint with Logan during the deep-dive.

Action items before Tuesday:
 - Laura/Logan: prepared to review memory/KV sizing assumptions + network egress profile (esp. for large generations).
 - Samira/Marty: confirm Tuesday 10:00 PT and share any procurement timelines/PO constraints we should be aware of.

I attached a short reference PDF with typical SKU trade-offs (redwood-dedicated-reference-kpi.pdf). We’ll run a concrete cost/latency estimate after the deep-dive and return two explicit pool configurations (cost-optimized and latency-optimized).

Thanks — talk Tuesday.
